children: Mysten Labs President Kevin Boon has succeeded Evan Cheng as CEO of the Sui Layer 1 blockchain developer. According to ChainCatcher, Cheng will remain chief technology officer and personally lead the company’s newly established internal AI division. In a public letter published on October 16, Cheng said Boon had accepted the role and announced the appointment on X. Boon previously served as Mysten Labs’ chief legal officer before becoming president; Cheng said he had planned for Boon to take over when he appointed him president.

The AI division will have its own engineering and product development functions, aiming to reduce reliance on external providers. Modeled on Mysten’s on-chain finance business unit, established this summer, it will focus on agent-trust products and AI-native infrastructure. Cheng said the leadership transition will give him more time for technical leadership while allowing him to continue supporting the Sui and Walrus ecosystems. The division aims to enable agents to carry out tasks autonomously within limits set by users, with products and services built around Sui and Walrus. Walrus, Mysten’s decentralized storage protocol, launched its mainnet in March 2025. Cheng also cited Verifiable Agent Arbiter, developed with Google Cloud and announced on October 6. The evidence layer is designed to help enterprises demonstrate that their AI agents operate within authorized limits. Under its design, detailed agent records remain in customer-controlled Google Cloud Storage, while cryptographic proofs are stored on Walrus and coordinated on Sui. Initial enterprise deployments are planned before broader availability.

title: Mysten Labs Names Kevin Boon CEO as Evan Cheng Remains CTO and Leads AI Division
